chapters.title: The Cold Edges of the World: Where the Opponents Are Cast
editorial_queries: The source lists the three forms of Aliyy — *Aliyyun*, *Aliyya*, *Aliyyi* — and then gives the diacritics in the order "zabar, zer, and pesh"; linguistically, *Aliyyun* carries *pesh* (dammah), *Aliyya* carries *zabar* (fathah), and *Aliyyi* carries *zer* (kasrah), so the stated order of diacritics does not match the listed order of forms — this may be an error in the source or a different convention of ordering, and was reproduced exactly as given.

The phrase "makes his soul out of his bodies" in the source is obscure; the articulation renders it as the Qudrat's gift drawing the soul upward and beyond the body, but the precise doctrinal meaning may warrant review by a subject-matter editor.
comprehension_flags: A modern reader unfamiliar with Ismaili cosmology may not follow the distinction between *ra's* and *dhanab* as imaginal (*wahmi*) loci versus the physical poles, or why this distinction determines the absence of namaz in polar regions — a note may help in a glossary or footnote pass.
"Qudrat" is used as a proper noun throughout without explanation; modern readers unfamiliar with Ismaili theological usage will not know it refers to Divine Power or Providence as an active force.
terminology_notes: *nafs al-hissiyyah* — standardize as "sensory soul" throughout, with the Arabic retained on first occurrence per passage.
"Allah taala" — the source uses this unhyphenated, unapostrophized form consistently; confirm this is the book-wide standard spelling before finalizing.
